children: China's new housing reforms could weigh on construction activity, says BofA Securities in a note. It is encouraging that manufacturing activity improved in August from July, BofA points out. "In particular, the notable rebound in new orders suggests a better near-term recovery outlook, likely led by large enterprises," it says. However, construction activity continued to remain weak. BofA says the housing reform announced last week, which requires future residential projects to be sold as completed homes or only after structural completion, could reduce developers' capital turnover. This may further weigh on property-related construction activity in the future, BofA says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
